items.stem: Define a) Health b) Mental health c) Social health
items.answer: a) Health: Health is a state of complete well-being and includes physical, mental, emotional and social health. b) Mental health: the chapter treats mental health as one of the components of that complete well-being, and states what is needed for it - students have to inculcate friendship between classmates and indulge in amicable behavior with others in school so that they develop a helpful nature, and these are necessary for mental and emotional health. c) Social health: Social health may be defined as the ability to form satisfying interpersonal relationships with others; one who is able to make positive relationships and acquires the ability to adapt in different social situations and act appropriately as per the situation concerned can be called a socially healthy person.

items.stem: What do you mean by life skills? Enlist them.
items.answer: Life skills are the skills that teachers should train students in, and all these life skills help to develop desirable social health and live happily in a society. They are: (1) Empathy - the ability to understand another person's feelings in a particular situation; (2) Self awareness - the recognition of a person's own character, strengths, areas of growth, beliefs and values; (3) Effective communication - having skills of communication that facilitate interaction with people in positive ways; (4) Interpersonal relationships - building relationships of friendship and goodwill with all others; (5) Problem solving - the ability to resolve challenges; (6) Decision making - the quality of analyzing problem to find and act to reach an appropriate solution; (7) Creative thinking - the ability to do something in a novel manner; (8) Critical thinking - the capacity to analyse multiple perspectives and objectively evaluate the same; (9) Coping with stress and emotional distress - the management and regulation of emotions and moments of stress.

items.stem: What are the characteristics of a socially healthy person?
items.answer: A socially healthy person has the ability to form satisfying interpersonal relationships with others, is able to make positive relationships and acquires the ability to adapt in different social situations and act appropriately as per the situation concerned. Being socially healthy, the person is able to develop interpersonal relations through maintaining equality, fraternity and justice. The socially healthy person makes an effort to contact and meet old friends, to remember enjoyable periods of childhood which can be a good way to beat stress and spend leisure time. Tolerance and appreciation are virtues in socially healthy individuals, and such a person has a desirable self image and self esteem and also self confidence, with the ability to live harmoniously in the society.

items.stem: Suggest three ways in which social health can be promoted in children by each of the following - a) School b) Teachers c) Family
items.answer: a) School: (1) the school should have a positive environment where children mingle with teachers, peer group and non-teaching staff without fear and apprehensions; (2) organise variety of co-curricular activities and interclass sport and games competitions, ensure participation of maximum number of students, train them in leadership as well as team spirit, and include a games period every working day in the time table; (3) encourage team games and adopt the House system, which helps children to interact with students of other classes too, and if there is a canteen, permit sale of healthy food like fruits or fruit juices. b) Teachers: (1) set an example, because students easily learn to be socially healthy if the teacher herself or himself sets an example rather than lecture on social health; (2) train students in learning life skills like empathy and self awareness, effective communication, problem-solving and decision-making, creative and critical thinking, and coping with stress and emotion; (3) have a friendly, stress-free atmosphere in class through group activities, which build team spirit and remove boredom, and discourage students from engaging in socially unhealthy practices such as vindictive attitudes, selfishness, jealousy and culture of hatred. c) Family: (1) guardians or parents are the prime teachers and caretakers, so they have to be aware themselves to be role model, and be cautious in what they do in front of children and how long they are in front of the TV, since watching of television for longer duration is bad for students; (2) feed children healthy food and make them aware of the benefits of enjoying nutritious food and a balanced diet, and encourage them to indulge in physical activity to build their muscles and bones; (3) the parents and elder family members need to guide them in social skills and be accessible to children for necessary guidance, guiding adolescents through advice, answering their queries and occupying them through activities to keep them away from involvement in addictive substances like tobacco, drugs and alcohol.

items.stem: What kind of society do you envisage if majority of its members are socially healthy?
items.answer: It would be a society that lives in harmony, because the socially healthy groups can live in harmony despite differing in opinions, and tolerance and appreciation are virtues in socially healthy individuals. Its members, being socially healthy, would be able to develop interpersonal relations through maintaining equality, fraternity and justice, and all the life skills they possess would help them to develop desirable social health and live happily in a society. In this manner students, teachers, parents and community will realise the benefits of being physically, mentally and socially healthy, and it would be a great way to build a healthy nation.
